title: Connecting Schema
strapline: Joining, tying, sticking, coupling the train carriages — and, just as gladly, pulling it all apart again.
intent: Recognise connecting as a schema — the drive to join things together, and the equal fascination with disconnecting them.
Understand the learning inside it: how parts fit and hold, cause and effect, sequences and simple mechanisms.
Read the endless coupling and uncoupling of train carriages, taping, tying and linking as real research.
Build the fine-motor precision of fitting, clicking, threading and fastening things together.
Support early relationships too, as connecting often becomes joining in — linking hands, joining play.
implementation: Offer things that join: train tracks and carriages, linking cubes, pop-beads, nuts and bolts, tape, string, pegs, magnetic tiles.
Provide things to join with — split pins, treasury tags, ribbon, sticky tape, pipe cleaners for the older toddlers.
Name the schema as you go ('you've connected all the carriages into one long train').
Value the taking-apart as much as the joining — disconnecting is the other half of the same enquiry.
Keep small connectors safely sized and supervised, and offer big chunky joiners for the youngest hands.
key_questions: How long can you make the train — how many will you connect?
Which piece will join on next?
How did you get them to stick together?
Can you pull them apart again — click!
Shall we join our tracks so the train can travel all the way round?

impact.text: A child joins and separates pieces, discovering how parts fit and hold — and come apart again.
Toddlers click, thread, tape and couple with growing precision, fine-motor control building with each join.
Connecting becomes cooperative — children link tracks, join carriages and play alongside on one shared line.
Sorting and matching emerge as toddlers group the pieces that join and line up what belongs together.

enhancements: Train track and magnetic carriages for endless coupling and uncoupling.
Big pop-beads and linking chains for the youngest joiners.
A construction crate of nuts, bolts and pre-drilled planks to bolt together.
A taping-and-tying station — masking tape, string, treasury tags and boxes to join.
Magnetic tiles for connecting into towers, walls and rooms.

playing_exploring: The child chooses what to join and what to pull apart, following their own connecting agenda.
Fitting and coupling are explored hands-on, by trial and by feel.
active_learning: Toddlers persist at fiddly joins, trying again until the pieces click and hold.
creating_thinking: Children plan a chain, a track or a train, holding the idea of the whole while they add each part.
